It depends. One back office saves time when shops share products and staff. Separate installs suit shops with very different catalogs. We explain this in the plan and suggest what fits.
Each shop domain must point to the same install, and your host must allow this. We check your hosting first and tell you if a change is needed.

Will modules work in every shop?
Most do, but some are not multistore aware. We test your key modules in each shop and flag any that need replacing before launch.

desc:
PrestaShop multistore, languages and currencies let you run several shops from one back office. Ecom Swift LLC plans what is shared and what stays separate, then configures each shop with its own domain, currency and rules.

## What is PrestaShop multistore?

PrestaShop multistore is a built in feature that lets one installation run several shops. Each shop can have its own domain, theme, language, currency, carriers and prices, while sharing a catalog, customers or stock where you choose. Staff manage everything from one back office and switch between shops or groups as needed.

Languages and currencies are related but separate. A single shop can offer several languages and currencies, and multistore adds the option of a distinct storefront for each market or brand.

## Why a rushed setup causes trouble

Multistore rewards planning and punishes guessing. If you share the wrong data, a price meant for one market appears in another. If stock is shared when it should be separate, one shop sells units that belong to the other. If tax and carrier rules are copied across without checking, customers see wrong totals at checkout.

Fixing these after launch means touching live orders and customer records. A written plan before the build keeps these decisions deliberate.

## How a good structure improves results

A good structure lets you serve different markets without duplicating your whole workload. You add a product once and make it available in each shop with its own price. Staff work in one place, and rules for tax, currency and delivery fit each audience. Customers see a store in their language, priced in their currency, with shipping options that make sense for them.

That clarity makes the buying path easier, and your team spends less time on copying and checking. How well a new market performs still depends on demand, language quality and marketing, which this service does not control.

## What a strong multistore setup includes

- A written sharing plan covering catalog, prices, stock, customers and carts.
- A separate domain and theme for each shop where you need them.
- Currency settings, with exchange rate handling agreed with you.
- Tax rules set per shop and per destination.
- Carriers and delivery zones configured shop by shop.
- Language packs installed and content structure ready for translation.
- Shop specific prices on a shared catalog.
- Rules for shared or separate stock.
- Staff roles limited to the shops each person manages.
- Test orders placed in every shop before launch.

## How we set it up

We begin with a short planning document. It lists each shop, its audience, which data is shared and which is separate. After you approve it, we build the structure on staging, so your live store is not disturbed.

We then configure each shop: domain, language, currency, theme, taxes and carriers. We place test orders through each shop and check how orders, customers and stock behave. The Basic package adds one extra shop or language with a sharing plan. Standard covers up to three shops with a shared catalog, shop prices, currency and tax rules, carriers and test orders. Premium covers a larger set of shops and languages, stock rules, staff access per shop, a training session and an admin guide.

We configure the structure. Translation of your product content is a separate task, and we can import translations you already have.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Decide early whether each shop is a separate brand or a regional version of one brand.
- Keep product codes consistent across all shops.
- Check that your hosting handles several domains.
- Review each module for multistore support before relying on it.
- Test the full order flow in every shop.

**Avoid:**
- Sharing customer accounts across shops without checking privacy and tax rules.
- Copying one shop's tax settings to another without review.
- Adding shops before the first one is stable.
- Translating by machine alone and publishing without a read-through.
- Giving every staff member access to every shop.

## Who this is for

This service suits sellers entering a second country who need local currency and language. It suits owners running two brands from one catalog. It also suits wholesalers who want a separate storefront with trade pricing next to a public retail shop.

## How to get started

Tell us which shops, languages and currencies you want, and what products they should share. Send your current domains and hosting details. Give us developer or staff access on staging and, once approved, on the live shop, never your passwords. We reply with a planning questionnaire and begin the build.
